findings.text: §21's deliverable joins a group-scoped rule (a member whose head is an ancestor is finished, left out of the candidate, and the group retires when all members are finished) to a queue-wide invariant ("a pointer is never written for a run whose ledger row records it promoted, by a group or by any other pending-landing record; a record that would do so is an obligation naming the record"), and the section's own evidence records only the group case, so the second deliverable has no recorded defect behind it, reaches §6's and §16's non-group records, and needs its own obligation and clearance rule — one node cannot be closed on one verdict for both
